record.title: Google DeepMind reports an Antigravity workflow for cheminformatics and macrocycle design
record.summary: Google DeepMind's 3 November walkthrough describes a human-steered Antigravity workflow for cheminformatics using a lung-cancer-treatment example. The company reports literature and catalog search across thousands of compounds, a curated view of 568 compounds, matched-pair analysis, potency models and proposed rigidified macrocycles with synthesis routes in about an hour. The report is first-party evidence of what Google describes, not independent confirmation of the run or its measurements. The source says the designs are hypotheses that require synthesis and experimental validation; it reports no such validation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Google DeepMind reports that its Cheminformatics Skills for Antigravity were used in a lung-cancer-treatment example to search literature and catalogs for thousands of compounds, curate compound data, perform matched molecular pair analysis, train potency models and propose rigidified macrocycles with suggested synthesis routes in about an hour.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The provider's walkthrough describes an interactive view of 568 curated compounds, held-out evaluation of multiple potency models, and analysis using a scaffold split. It attributes the workflow to a model orchestrating database and analysis tools while deterministic chemistry tools perform molecular calculations.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The post does not establish that any proposed molecule was synthesized or experimentally validated, that the reported potency predictions are accurate, that the workflow is independently reproducible, or that it is faster or more effective than a matched human-led workflow.

evidence_gaps.description: The proposed macrocycles and routes have no reported synthesis or experimental validation in the inspected source; the source states that each design requires synthesis and experimental validation.
No independent run, full run logs, error analysis, or matched human-led workflow measurement was inspected; the qualitative timing comparison is provider-reported.

brief.importance_rationale: If representative, an agentic workflow that links scientific literature extraction, compound-data curation, predictive modeling and synthesis planning could change the iteration throughput of computational chemistry. This moderate consequence score reflects the potential workflow significance if true, not confidence in the provider's account, validated potency, or evidence of faster drug discovery.
limitations: The evidence is one Google DeepMind walkthrough, not an independent evaluation.
The article does not report synthesis or experimental assay results for the proposed designs and explicitly calls them testable hypotheses.
No task-level error rate, human-led baseline, measured time comparison or complete run log is provided.
The linked repository README establishes that a public science-skills bundle exists, but the specific cheminformatics skill files and this exact workflow were not inspected or reproduced.

relationships.summary: A distinct cheminformatics workflow example from the same provider follows its October antimicrobial-peptide workflow report; neither article establishes independent workflow performance.

technical.claimed_result: Google DeepMind reports that Antigravity's Cheminformatics Skills helped search, curate and analyze compounds and propose macrocycles and synthesis routes in about an hour.
technical.compute_or_cost: No model usage, compute cost, experiment cost or measured staff-time comparison is reported.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected primary source demonstrates that Google DeepMind published this workflow account and its stated limitations. the research desk did not independently reproduce the workflow, inspect complete run artifacts, synthesize compounds or verify predicted potency.
technical.mechanism: The post describes a language model coordinating literature/database navigation and scientific reasoning, while deterministic chemistry tools handle molecular calculations. The workflow uses RDKit and connectors to ChEMBL and PubChem, followed by matched-pair analysis, potency modeling and proposed synthesis planning.
technical.regime: One provider-authored example concerning compounds related to crizotinib and lorlatinib. Google reports thousands of compounds searched and a 568-compound interactive curated set; it does not provide a matched human baseline or broader validated dataset.
technical.reproducibility: Not assessed by the research desk. A public science-skills repository was located, but its cheminformatics skill files, exact revision, data snapshot and run trace were not inspected.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched human-led or alternative-agent baseline is reported. The post qualitatively says a comparable workflow typically takes multiple days.

brief.title: Google DeepMind reports an Antigravity workflow for cheminformatics and macrocycle design
brief.why_it_matters: Scientific workflows often require linking literature, databases, molecular analysis and predictive modeling. If independently validated, agentic coordination of these steps could change how computational chemists prepare and test design hypotheses. The inspected post reports one company-run example, not measured general productivity or a validated drug candidate, and it says synthesis and experimental testing remain necessary.

other.title: Google DeepMind reports a human-steered Antigravity workflow for antimicrobial-peptide candidate search
other.summary: Google DeepMind’s 15 October walkthrough describes a researcher-steered Antigravity/Gemini 3.8 Flash workflow that searches UniProt candidates, cross-checks sequence similarity, compares predicted structures and genomic context, and prepares a wet-lab protocol. The example names UniProt A0A0U0D591, a 97-amino-acid protein assigned to the Lactococcin 972 family; the company says the candidate and others are undergoing wet-lab validation. This is a first-party account of a computational candidate-selection workflow, not evidence of antibacterial efficacy or independent discovery performance.
